checks.note: Dedicated clinic-agent SA in its own namespace, mapped by IRSA to clinic-agent-runtime. The only other SA bound to that role (clinic-agent-reminders) is the same agent's CronJob worker, not an unrelated service. No other deployment in the repo uses these names.

Every client credential is obtained via the agent's own role (Secrets Manager per-clinic secrets for EHR, payments and SMS) or the agent's projected workload token (eligibility). The only incoming Authorization header, in webchat.ts, is verified and used to identify the subject. It is never forwarded to any client.

The user is carried in a separate RunContext.subject field, while the agent identity and workload token stay the agent's. Weakness: in eligibility-a2a.ts the patient appears only in the scope string and subject_token is the agent's own token. That is not a true act/sub exchange, but it does not replace the agent identity or forward the user's token.
The runtime role trusts only the agent's service-account subjects and carries the agent's policies, with no user or group binding. Revoking it cuts the agent's AWS access without touching any user.

note: I found no failing control; the main weakness is that the eligibility token exchange encodes the patient only in the scope string rather than as a true delegated subject.
